{{short description|American computer programmer and independent investigator}}
'''Glen Jay Kuban''' (born 1957)<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://paleo.cc/paluxy/gkbio.htm |title=My Background |website=Glen Kuban website}}</ref> is an American computer programmer and independent investigator from [[Brunswick, Ohio]]. He is known for his work in [[Paluxy River]] dinosaur footprints.

Kuban became interested in studying dinosaur footprints in 1980 when he began studying the Paluxy River prints, which he had expected to be human. After studying these prints and conducting field work on them he confirmed the results of an earlier study by creation scientists from [[Loma Linda University]]<ref>Neufeld, Berney, 1975, Dinosaur Tracks and Giant Men. Origins, Vol. 2, No. 2, pp. 64-76</ref> that they appeared to be dinosaurian, not human. One reason he reached this conclusion was that the prints had shallow indentations that corresponded to dinosaurian toes, not human ones,<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.asa3.org/ASA/PSCF/1988/PSCF9-88Hastings.html | title=The Rise and Fall of the Paluxy Mantracks | publisher=[[American Scientific Affiliation]] | work=[[Perspectives on Science and Christian Faith]] | date=September 1988 | accessdate=14 June 2017 | author=Hastings, Ronnie J.}}</ref> and detailed analysis of the distinctive colorations in each purportedly human print revealed these prints to be dinosaurian.<ref name=nyt/> After cleaning and mapping the trails during his field work there, he tried, unsuccessfully, to convince certain creationists to look at them.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://ncse.com/cej/5/1/tracking-those-incredible-creationists | title=Tracking Those Incredible Creationists | publisher=[[National Center for Science Education]] | work=[[Creation/Evolution]] | date=Winter 1985 | accessdate=14 June 2017 | author=Hastings, Ronnie J.}}</ref> After carefully studying the tracks, he determined that all of the purportedly human prints there were actually dinosaurian, writing, "I have concluded that no genuine human tracks have been found in the Paluxy riverbed."<ref name=nyt>{{cite web | url=https://www.nytimes.com/1986/06/17/science/fossils-of-man-tracks-shown-to-be-dinosaurian.html | title=Fossils of 'Man Tracks' Shown to Be Dinosaurian | work=[[The New York Times]] | date=17 June 1986 | accessdate=14 June 2017 | author=Wilford, John Noble | authorlink=John Noble Wilford}}</ref> [http://paleo.cc/paluxy/onheel.htm Kuban was the first to identify the larger imprint as the impression of the metatarsal bones.]
